patterns.what_worked: Verifying the two lanes against the client source instead of their own reports was the highest-value move: every load-bearing API claim in T1 was re-read on origin/forever (no SecretWhen* on GetSpellCooldownDuration, no SecretArgumentsAddAspect on SetCooldownFromDurationObject, NeverSecret isOnGCD/isActive, HasSecretValues ReturnsNeverSecret, allowUntaintedCreation + DisableUntrustedLayoutScriptsTemplate, the exact formatter enum members the code passes, initializeFrame running before access restrictions), so the audit rests on the branch rather than on trust. Two independent proofs made the secret-flow verdict concrete: (1) with HasSecretValues()==true and every object getter raising, compat returns 0,0,0,0,true and the new helper returns the handle without calling a getter (259 checks, 0 failed); (2) truncating the new sections out of copies of the two extended suites yields exactly the pre-lane check counts (893 and 177), which is how I proved no pre-existing check was deleted or weakened without a diff. The mutation re-run reproduced all 20 claimed mutants with identical counts and the declared survivor, and one extra mutant of mine showed the pre-existing HasSecretValues guard is pinned (not an untested secret path).
patterns.what_was_hard: The brief forbids git in this repo, so there is no historical diff for behaviour preservation; I substituted (a) a source-level read of every numeric branch, (b) check-count parity of the pre-existing suites, and (c) the mutation table - and disclosed that residual in the report. The other hard part is the environment: every bash call gets a private /tmp, so the copy + mutant + suite + cleanup must live inside one call (the trap T1 and t3 recorded); the first attempt to reuse a /tmp copy across calls silently lost it. Also worth knowing for the next verifier: the trivial try of a mutation can fail for the wrong reason if the asserting helper returns a table (my first V1 probe destructured pcall's returns wrongly); always read the failure text.
patterns.skill_gap: No client, so the last mile stays open: whether the engine accepts and renders a secret-valued LuaDurationObject from a tainted caller (U3/U5) and whether the Mainline GCD probe spell 61304 exists on Forever (U7/F8). My own two findings that no offline test can currently catch (F3 named-container retry after a post-creation setup failure; F4 resize denial while auras are secret) need injectors the aura suite does not have yet.
